construct: The thick ascending limb is relatively impermeable to water and actively reabsorbs NaCl through apical NKCC2. Repeated separation of salt from water along the loop of Henle creates and amplifies the corticomedullary osmotic gradient. Blocking NKCC2 reduces medullary interstitial hypertonicity and limits maximal urine concentration even when vasopressin is present.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Maximal urine concentration requires a corticomedullary osmotic gradient generated in large part by active NaCl reabsorption through NKCC2 in the water-impermeable thick ascending limb.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Collecting-duct AQP2 is necessary for water reabsorption, but the stem explicitly preserves vasopressin and AQP2; the defect is loss of the medullary gradient.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Selective NKCC2 inhibition with intact vasopressin/AQP2 uniquely points to reduced TAL NaCl accumulation in the medullary interstitium.
